title: Northgate Card Billing-Error Resolution Limits — Noncompliance Allowance on Settled Duplicate Disputes
content:
A duplicate-posting dispute about a Northgate order on a **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account that is settled for the cardholder after its resolution limit has passed carries a noncompliance allowance, credited to the cardholder with the settlement.

**Resolution limit.** The dispute is past its resolution limit when the most recent statement on the account closed before today and at least the tier's maximum resolution cycles in whole calendar months after the notice date, or when more than the tier's maximum resolution days have passed from the notice date to today. The most recent statement on the account is the statement with the latest closing date; the notice date is the date the dispute notice was received; the maximum resolution cycles and days are the tier's billing-rights figures (2 cycles and 90 days on every Northgate Card).

**Allowance.** The noncompliance allowance follows the resolution limit:

- where the dispute is past its resolution limit and the correct part is at least the noncompliance amount of this rule, 50.00 USD, the noncompliance allowance is that noncompliance amount, 50.00 USD;
- where the dispute is past its resolution limit and the correct part is below 50.00 USD, the noncompliance allowance is the correct part;
- in every other case there is no noncompliance allowance.

The correct part of the dispute is the disputed amount less the duplicate excess, and never less than zero; the duplicate excess is the amount by which the purchase postings carrying the order's reference exceed what the order record charged, never less than zero.

| Past the resolution limit | Correct part | Allowance |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 50.00 or more | 50.00 |
| yes | below 50.00 (zero included) | the correct part |
| no | any | none |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical dates and amounts)

- Notice received on the 10th of a month; the most recent statement closed on the 10th two months later, before today: two whole calendar months, so the limit has passed. Had it closed on the 9th, only one whole month would have passed, and the limit would turn on the day count alone.
- Notice received 90 days before today: not more than 90 days, so the day test is not met; 91 days before today: the day test is met.
- Past the limit, disputed amount 120.00, duplicate excess 50.00: correct part 70.00, allowance 50.00. Disputed amount 120.00, duplicate excess 100.00: correct part 20.00, allowance 20.00. Duplicate excess 120.00: correct part 0.00, allowance 0.00.
